q: The sea water contains many salts such as ____, potassium chloride, magnesium sulphate, magnesium chloride and magnesium bromide.
e: The sea water contains many salts such as sodium chloride, potassium chloride, magnesium sulphate, magnesium chloride and magnesium bromide. Sodium chloride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (____), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (limestone), etc.
e: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (limestone), etc. Epsom salt is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (____), etc.
e: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (limestone), etc. Limestone is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A salt is produced when an acid reacts with a ____.
e: A salt is produced when an acid reacts with a base. A base reacts with an acid to give a salt and water.

q: The salt consists of two parts. One part comes from the base, the other from the ____.
e: The salt consists of two parts. One part comes from the base, the other from the acid. Acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The sodium ion ($Na^+$) part of the salt comes from the base and the chloride ion ($Cl^-$) comes from the ____.
e: The sodium ion (Na+) part of the salt comes from the base and the chloride ion (Cl-) comes from the acid. Acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When an acid reacts with a base, a salt and water are formed. This reaction is known as ____.
e: When an acid reacts with a base, a salt and water are formed. This reaction is known as neutralisation. Neutralisation is acid plus base making salt and water.

q: It involves the combination of $H^+$ ion produced from acid and $OH^-$ ion produced from base to form ____.
e: It involves the combination of H+ ion produced from acid and OH- ion produced from base to form water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Neutralisation reaction occurs in our stomach. The acid (HCl) produced by our stomach, is so strong that it is ____ with a base produced by cells.
e: Neutralisation reaction occurs in our stomach. The acid (HCl) produced by our stomach, is so strong that it is neutralised with a base produced by cells. Neutralised is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Salts are also produced when an acid reacts with a metal or a metal ____.
e: Salts are also produced when an acid reacts with a metal or a metal carbonate. Carbonate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: hydrochloric acid HCl produces ____ salts.
e: Hydrochloric acid HCl produces chloride salts. Chloride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: sulphuric acid $H_2SO_4$ produces ____ salts.
e: Sulphuric acid H2SO4 produces sulphate salts. Sulphate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: nitric acid $HNO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: Nitric acid HNO3 produces nitrate salts. Nitrate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: sulphurous acid $H_2SO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: Sulphurous acid H2SO3 produces sulphite salts. Sulphite is the idea that completes this fact.

q: carbonic acid $H_2CO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: Carbonic acid H2CO3 produces carbonate salts. Carbonate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ethanoic acid $CH_3COOH$ produces ____ salt.
e: Ethanoic acid CH3COOH produces ethanoate salt. Ethanoate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: all ____ are soluble.
e: All nitrates are soluble. Nitrates is the idea that completes this fact.

q: all chlorides are soluble except silver, mercury(I), ____.
e: All chlorides are soluble except silver, mercury(I), lead(II). Lead(II) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: all sulphates are soluble except ____, lead(II), calcium.
e: All sulphates are soluble except barium, lead(II), calcium. Barium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: carbonates of sodium, potassium and ____ are soluble.
e: Carbonates of sodium, potassium and ammonium are soluble. Ammonium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The preparation method depends on whether the salt is ____ in water or not.
e: The preparation method depends on whether the salt is soluble in water or not. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soluble salts are usually prepared by ____ method.
e: Soluble salts are usually prepared by crystallisation method. Crystallisation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Insoluble salts are usually prepared by ____ method.
e: Insoluble salts are usually prepared by precipitation method. Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid from a solution.

q: Salts of sodium, potassium and ammonium can be prepared from caustic soda solution (NaOH), caustic potash solution (KOH) and ammonia solution ($NH_4OH$), respectively, by the ____ using the appropriate acid.
e: Salts of sodium, potassium and ammonium can be prepared from caustic soda solution (NaOH), caustic potash solution (KOH) and ammonia solution (NH4OH), respectively, by the neutralisation using the appropriate acid. Neutralisation is acid plus base making salt and water.

q: Insoluble salts are prepared by ____.
e: Insoluble salts are prepared by precipitation. Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid from a solution.

q: A ____ precipitate of barium sulphate, $BaSO_4$, is formed.
e: A white precipitate of barium sulphate, BaSO4, is formed. White is the idea that completes this fact.

q: sodium chloride NaCl is used as a food ____.
e: Sodium chloride NaCl is used as a food additive. Additive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: sodium sulphate $Na_2SO_4$, sodium nitrite $NaNO_2$, sodium citrate $Na_3C_6H_5O_7$ are used as food ____.
e: Sodium sulphate Na2SO4, sodium nitrite NaNO2, sodium citrate Na3C6H5O7 are used as food preservatives. Preservatives is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ammonium sulphate $(NH_4)_2SO_4$, ammonium nitrate $NH_4NO_3$, ammonium phosphate $(NH_4)_3PO_4$ are used as ____.
e: Ammonium sulphate (NH4)2SO4, ammonium nitrate NH4NO3, ammonium phosphate (NH4)3PO4 are used as fertilisers. Fertilisers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: potassium chloride KCl is used as a ____.
e: Potassium chloride KCl is used as a fertiliser. Fertiliser is the idea that completes this fact.

q: magnesium sulphate $MgSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O$ is used for medical uses (____).
e: Magnesium sulphate MgSO4 7H2O is used for medical uses (Epsom salt). Epsom salt is the idea that completes this fact.

q: magnesium hydroxide $Mg(OH)_2$ is used for medical uses (____, MOM).
e: Magnesium hydroxide Mg(OH)2 is used for medical uses (milk of magnesia, MOM). Milk of magnesia is the idea that completes this fact.

q: calcium sulphate $CaSO_4$ is used for medical uses (____, POP).
e: Calcium sulphate CaSO4 is used for medical uses (Plaster of Paris, POP). Plaster of Paris is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A salt is a substance produced from the reaction between an acid and a base or a ____.
e: A salt is a substance produced from the reaction between an acid and a base or a metal. Metal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Based on the ____, salts can be classified as chlorides, sulphates, nitrates, sulphites and carbonates, etc.
e: Based on the acids, salts can be classified as chlorides, sulphates, nitrates, sulphites and carbonates, etc. Acids is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soluble salts are usually prepared from the reactions between metals and dilute acids followed by ____.
e: Soluble salts are usually prepared from the reactions between metals and dilute acids followed by crystallisation. Crystallisation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Insoluble salts are usually prepared by ____ method.
e: Insoluble salts are usually prepared by precipitation method. Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid from a solution.

q: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and ____ only.
e: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water only. Water is the idea that completes this fact.
